LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 10.1.1 IMPROMPTU SPEECHES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 10.1.1 Impromptu Speeches
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 10.1.1 Impromptu Speeches, part of Strand 10 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do we make an impromptu speech?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 10.1.1 Impromptu Speeches together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital literacy: Learner interacts with technology as they make a recording of the speech.

• Self-efficacy: Learner organises their own work as they prepare and delivers impromptu speeches at short notice.

• Collaboration: Learner develops speaking or signing skills as he/she uses the plenary discussions to sharpen their

communication skills.

Values:
• Responsibility: the learner makes speeches on an issue like responsible use of social and mass media.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate the concept of social and mass media learnt in English to proper use of social and mass media in

Social Studies.

Suggested Learning Resources

Class readers, Adapted Course books, Flash cards, Recording devices e.g. tablets and mobile phones, Dictionary, Internet,
